chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

A man from the Anṣār came to my father عليه السلام and said: 'I have been afflicted with a grave matter. I had a slave-girl with whom I used to have relations. I had relations with her one day, then went out for a need of mine after performing ghusl (ritual bath) from her. I forgot some provision of mine, so I returned home to take it, and found my غلام on her belly. Then I counted for her from that day of mine nine months, and she gave birth to a girl.'

So he said: 'It is not fitting for you to approach her, nor to sell her. Rather, spend on her from your wealth as long as you remain alive; then instruct at your death that provision be spent on her from your wealth until Allah makes for you and for her an outlet.'

key_terms.أَنْفِقْ عَلَيْهَا مِنْ مَالِكَ: provide for her financially from your wealth
key_terms.لَا يَنْبَغِي لَكَ أَنْ تَقْرَبَهَا: you should not approach her sexually
key_terms.مَخْرَجًا: a way out or resolution granted by Allah
key_terms.ٱغْتَسَلْتُ: I performed ghusl (ritual bath) after intercourse

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when the paternity of a slave-girl’s child is uncertain?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling concerning a slave-girl whose child’s paternity became uncertain after both her master and his غلام had intercourse with her in a time frame that created doubt. The Imam عليه السلام forbids the man from approaching or selling her, and orders that she be maintained financially, reflecting caution in matters of lineage, sexual relations, and the rights of a vulnerable woman.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5677 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"A man from the Ansar came to my father (as) and said: 'I have been afflicted with a great matter. I had a maid whom I used to have relations with. One day, after being intimate with her, I went out for some of my needs after performing ghusl. I later realized I had forgotten some of my provisions, so I returned home to retrieve them and found my servant lying with her.
I then counted nine months from that day, and she gave birth to a girl.'

My father (as) said: 'It is not appropriate for you to approach her nor to sell her. However, spend on her from your wealth as long as you are alive, and when you die, bequeath that she continues to be provided for from your wealth until Allah (swt) grants you and her a way out.'"
